sources.title: Build a REST API with FastAPI: Routes, Errors, Pydantic Models

steps.title: Install FastAPI and run hello world
steps.instructions: Run `pip install fastapi uvicorn`, create main.py with `app = FastAPI()` and a `@app.get("/")` root function returning {"Hello": "World"}. Start it with `uvicorn main:app --reload` and open http://127.0.0.1:8000 to see the JSON.

targets.caption: Create the FastAPI app instance
Decorator defining the GET route at the root path
Server is up; open this URL in the browser
The JSON returned by the root route

explanations.topic: Uvicorn is the server that runs FastAPI apps
The @app.get decorator maps the GET method and a path to a function
uvicorn main:app means file name : app variable
--reload restarts the server when the file changes

hints: Install both packages first: FastAPI for the framework and Uvicorn for the server.
In main.py, import FastAPI, create app = FastAPI(), and decorate a function with @app.get("/") that returns a dict.
Run uvicorn from the folder containing main.py: uvicorn main:app --reload.
Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in the browser. You should see {"Hello":"World"}.
common_mistakes: Installing only fastapi and getting 'uvicorn: command not found'.
Running uvicorn from a different directory, which fails with 'Could not import module "main"'.
Using the wrong module:variable pair, e.g. uvicorn main --reload or uvicorn app:main.
Naming the instance something other than app but still running main:app ('Attribute "app" not found').
Forgetting the parentheses in FastAPI() or the leading slash in @app.get("/").

steps.title: Add POST endpoint to create items
steps.instructions: Add a module-level `items = []` list and a `@app.post("/items")` function `create_item(item: str)` that appends the item and returns the list. Test with `curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple'`.

targets.caption: Module-level list holding items
POST endpoint at /items
item is read as a query parameter
Server log: the POST request succeeded

explanations.topic: Creating an in-memory list to store to-do items
POST request to the /items path triggers create_item
A plain str function argument becomes a query parameter
Returning the whole list to see accumulated results
Testing the endpoint with curl and a ?item= query string

hints: Define an empty list at module level, above your endpoint functions, so it persists between requests.
Use the @app.post("/items") decorator, not @app.get, since you are adding data.
Declare the parameter as item: str. FastAPI treats simple typed arguments as query parameters, so pass it as ?item=apple in the URL.
Inside the function call items.append(item) and then return items; keep uvicorn running (with --reload) in another terminal while you curl.
common_mistakes: Using @app.get instead of @app.post, so curl -X POST returns 405 Method Not Allowed.
Defining items = [] inside the function, which resets the list on every request.
Sending the item in a JSON body instead of the ?item= query string, which gives a 422 'field required' error.
Forgetting to quote the URL in the shell, so ? or & get interpreted by the shell.
Not restarting uvicorn (or not using --reload), so the new route returns 404 Not Found.

steps.title: Add GET endpoint with path parameter
steps.instructions: Add `@app.get("/items/{item_id}")` with `get_item(item_id: int)` returning `items[item_id]`. Re-add items (the list resets on reload), then curl /items/0 and /items/1.

targets.caption: New GET endpoint with a path parameter
Server log for curl /items/0 and /items/1

explanations.topic: Path parameters in curly braces become function arguments
Server reload resets the in-memory items list
Path value maps to the function parameter by name
Type hints let FastAPI convert the path value to int
Out-of-range index causes an internal server error

hints: Add a new route decorated with @app.get whose path contains a variable in curly braces, e.g. /items/{item_id}.
The function parameter must have the same name as the path variable, and annotate it as int so it can index the list.
Return items[item_id] from the function. Saving the file reloads the server and empties the list, so POST a couple of items again before testing.
Test with: curl -X GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/items/0, which should print the first item you added.
common_mistakes: Testing right after saving without re-adding items. The reload resets items to [], so /items/0 raises an IndexError (500).
Naming the function parameter differently from {item_id} in the path, so FastAPI treats it as a query parameter.
Omitting the int type hint, so item_id arrives as a string and indexing the list fails.
Using path "/items/item_id" without curly braces, which makes it a literal path.
Requesting an index beyond the list length and assuming the code is broken. The resulting 500 error is expected here and gets handled in the next step.

steps.title: Raise 404 with HTTPException
steps.instructions: Import HTTPException from fastapi and in get_item return the item if item_id < len(items), otherwise raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=...). Curl a missing index and confirm the 404 detail message.

targets.caption: Import HTTPException from fastapi at the top of the file
Return the item only when the index exists
Otherwise raise a 404 with a helpful detail
Curl a missing index to see the 404 detail

explanations.topic: Why an unhandled IndexError becomes a 500 Internal Server Error
HTTP status codes: 4xx client errors and 404 Not Found
HTTPException status_code and detail parameters

hints: Look at what happens when item_id is beyond the end of your items list. Check the index before you use it.
Add HTTPException to your import line: from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException.
Wrap the lookup in: if item_id < len(items): return items[item_id], else raise an exception.
else: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {item_id} not found"). Then rerun curl with an index that doesn't exist.
common_mistakes: Using `return HTTPException(...)` instead of `raise`, which sends a 200 response with the exception serialized in the body.
Forgetting to import HTTPException, which causes a NameError (500) on the missing-item request.
Using `<=` instead of `<` in the bounds check, so the last+1 index still raises IndexError.
Forgetting the `f` prefix on the detail string, so the output reads literally "Item {item_id} not found".
Not restarting uvicorn (or not running it with --reload), so curl still returns the old Internal Server Error.
Curling a missing index after a server restart cleared the in-memory items list, then being confused that every index returns 404.

steps.title: List items with limit query parameter
steps.instructions: In main.py add `@app.get("/items")` with `list_items(limit: int = 10)` returning `items[0:limit]`. Add several items, then curl `/items?limit=3` and `/items` to compare the JSON lists.

targets.caption: New list_items endpoint with a limit query parameter
Request with limit=3 returns the first 3 items

explanations.topic: Query parameters are automatically converted to the annotated type (int)
limit slices the list; default of 10 used when omitted
Same /items path, different HTTP method routes to a different function
Default value comes from the function signature

hints: Add a new function decorated with @app.get("/items") — same path as your POST endpoint, different method.
Give the function a parameter limit: int = 10; any function parameter not in the path becomes a query parameter.
Return items[0:limit] to slice the list.
POST several items first, then curl '/items?limit=3' (quote the URL) and '/items' to compare.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the type hint, so limit arrives as a string and slicing raises a TypeError.
Not quoting the URL in curl, so the shell interprets '?' or '&'.
Testing after a server restart without re-adding items, getting an empty list.
Defining the route with @app.post instead of @app.get, so GET returns 405 Method Not Allowed.

steps.title: Use a Pydantic Item model
steps.instructions: Import BaseModel from pydantic and define a model class with a required text: str and is_done: bool = False; make create_item take the model and get_item return it. POST JSON with curl and confirm a payload without text fails validation.

targets.caption: The Pydantic model with text and is_done
create_item now takes the model from the JSON body
Response object conforms to the model

explanations.topic: Pydantic models structure data and add validation
Model arguments are read from the JSON body, not query params
Default value is_done=False fills in when omitted
Removing a default makes a field required and validated

hints: Import BaseModel from pydantic and subclass it for your Item.
Give the model two fields: text: str (no default) and is_done: bool = False.
Change create_item's parameter to item: Item and annotate get_item with -> Item.
Send data as JSON: curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"text":"apple"}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/items (no ?item= query).
common_mistakes: Still sending the item as a ?item=apple query parameter, which now returns a 422 error.
Forgetting the Content-Type: application/json header in curl.
Leaving a default on text (e.g. text: str = None), so missing text doesn't fail validation.
Writing Is_done or is_done: bool without = False, making it required.
Using double quotes around the -d JSON in a shell without escaping inner quotes.

steps.title: Add response models to endpoints
steps.instructions: In main.py, add `response_model=Item` to the get_item decorator and `response_model=list[Item]` to the list_items decorator. Let uvicorn reload and confirm the endpoints still return Item-shaped JSON.

targets.caption: Declare the single-item response shape on the GET-by-id route
Declare a list-of-items response shape on the list route

explanations.topic: Modeling responses with the same Pydantic BaseModel used for requests
response_model is a decorator argument, not a function parameter
response_model tells clients/front-ends the response schema

hints: The response model goes in the route decorator, not in the function signature.
Add response_model=Item inside @app.get(...) for the endpoint that returns one item.
For the list endpoint, wrap the model in list: response_model=list[Item].
Save and let uvicorn --reload restart; then hit /items/0 and /items?limit=2 to confirm the JSON matches Item fields.
common_mistakes: Passing response_model as a function parameter instead of a decorator keyword argument.
Using response_model=Item on the list endpoint, causing a validation error because a list is returned.
Writing list[Item] on Python < 3.9 instead of List[Item] from typing.
Returning a plain string or dict missing required Item fields, which now fails response validation with a 500 error.
Forgetting to import or define Item above the routes, causing a NameError on reload.

steps.title: Explore interactive API docs
steps.instructions: With `uvicorn main:app --reload` running, open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs and use 'Try it out' then 'Execute' on POST /items. Also visit /redoc and /openapi.json.

targets.caption: Click 'Try it out' on POST /items to edit the request body
Execute sends the real request and shows the curl command and response body
The small link to the raw OpenAPI schema JSON

explanations.topic: FastAPI auto-generates interactive docs for free
Swagger UI at /docs lists endpoints, methods and parameters
Execute shows the curl command and actually sends the request
/redoc is an alternative docs view
openapi.json describes all paths, schemas and responses for client generation

hints: Make sure your uvicorn server is still running, then add /docs to the end of the server URL in your browser.
Expand the POST /items endpoint, click 'Try it out', and edit the example request body to match your Item model.
Click Execute and scroll down to see the curl command and the Response body.
Try http://127.0.0.1:8000/redoc and click the small /openapi.json link (or visit it directly).
common_mistakes: Server not running (or stopped by a syntax error), so /docs fails to load.
Forgetting to click 'Try it out', so the request body stays read-only.
Sending a request body that does not match the Pydantic Item model, which returns a 422 validation error.
Typing /doc or /redocs instead of /docs and /redoc and getting 404 Not Found.
Using a different port than the one uvicorn printed.
